question: what realised honesty rate maximises total sales against the real field, and does Kamenica-Gentzkow's q* survive contact with it?

q_star.formula: q* = p*(v - price) / ((1 - p)*(price - u)), clipped to [0,1]; u = 0 in every observed config
q_star.assumption_that_fails: K-G derives q* under seller COMMITMENT to a signal structure announced before the state is drawn. GLEE gives the seller no commitment device, so the buyer prices the realised record, not the announced rule.

what_the_agent_actually_does.reading: pers_lie_shading and pers_honest_rounds bind ONLY in the 'lie budget' branch, 1956 of 11599 non-trivial seller turns = 17%. In stratum A the code takes 'prior alone justifies purchase' and recommends unconditionally, so the realised lie rate is 1.000 for champion, conceder AND hardliner alike.
what_the_agent_actually_does.consequence: the honesty experiment the fleet believes it is running has never been run in stratum A or hidden-v, which together are 66% of our seller games

design_1_exogenous_lie_count_in_stratum_.why_causal: in stratum A all three deterministic probes recommend every unit, so lies_told == lows_so_far == Binomial(t-1, 1-p): exogenous noise given (round, p)
design_1_exogenous_lie_count_in_stratum_.reading: monotone decline WITHIN round block. Each lie costs about 0.32 in the log-odds of every later purchase, inside the stratum where K-G says the buyer should buy unconditionally.

design_2_randomized_seller_messages.why_causal: the randomized probe's seller recommends on a coin flip independent of quality and history: a genuine randomized experiment on the field buyer

effect_of_recommending_a_LOW_unit_all_st.note: figures from the 49-game snapshot; the immediate effect is precise, the future effect is not

by_state.units: change in total sales from that round onward; all CIs cross zero except the immediate components

design_2_randomized_seller_messages.verdict: the randomized experiment CANNOT resolve the future cost of a lie at n=71 games. To pin the total effect to +-0.25 sales needs roughly 420 randomized seller games; to +-0.10 needs about 2,600.

design_3_early_warnings.question: does an early honest warning buy trust that pays later?
design_3_early_warnings.design: randomized-probe seller games; the number of warnings in the first k rounds is a coin flip
design_3_early_warnings.verdict: NO support. All three point estimates are negative. But the randomized probe also warns on 49% of HIGH units, so its warnings are themselves uninformative; this is not a test of a TRUTHFUL warning. The CIs still admit the +0.025/warning the structural model needs.

policy_evaluation_stratum_A.method: simulate the exogenously-identified dose-response forward; P(buy|warn) = 0.283 measured in stratum A; uncertainty by refitting on 300 game-cluster bootstrap resamples and re-simulating
policy_evaluation_stratum_A.baseline: always recommend == q* = 1 == what champion, conceder and hardliner all actually do in stratum A
policy_evaluation_stratum_A.reading: K-G's q*=1 is beaten by an honest opening in 96% of bootstrap draws, but the 95% interval on the gain still contains zero. Never-lying is WORSE than q*=1 with 94% confidence. The optimum is interior and closer to q* than to honesty.

independent_structural_check.method: the field-buyer response model of persuasion_field_buyer_response_v1, simulated over all 15 config cells
independent_structural_check.agreement: both methods rank an honest opening above pure q* and both rank never-lying last or near-last; they disagree about the mechanism (the structural model credits warnings with building trust, which design 3 does not corroborate)

hidden_v_games.current_rule: recommend while the buyer's running buy rate >= 0.5
hidden_v_games.verdict: cannot tell. Game-level sold rate has sd 0.45 (games are bimodal: the buyer engages or does not), so 1,282 games per arm are needed for 80% power at delta = 0.05.

recommended_experiment.what: force an honest opening in stratum A and hidden-v: recommend only high-quality units for the first H rounds, then apply the existing lie budget. Test H in {0, 6, 10}.
recommended_experiment.why_not_an_arm_comparison: comparing arm-level sold rates needs ~1,160 stratum-A games per arm. The round-level dose-response is powered at 81 games and already significant.
recommended_experiment.how_to_analyse: refit the stratum-A logit of P(buy|recommend) on lies_told with round and config controls; H is exogenous by construction so lies_told stays exogenous. To halve the CI on the -0.323 coefficient needs about 324 stratum-A seller games, i.e. roughly 2,800 further persuasion games at the current config mix.

expected_size_if_the_point_estimate_hold.honest_note: SMALL. Stratum A is only 57 of 301 matched seller games and our percentile curve is flat there. This fix is worth doing because it is free, not because it closes the gap.
